label: Late original-phase position / delimiter (ramps up through the input, peaks at <DEL>)
explanation: Fires during the input-reading part of the sequence: never at t=0-1, weakly at t=2-3, and with increasing rate at later original positions (rate 0.17 at orig_idx 3 up to 0.88 at orig_idx 8), then most reliably at the <DEL> step (rate 0.73, 36% of mass). Essentially silent in the copy phase (89 activations out of 2.7M steps). Within a sequence the activation usually ramps up monotonically step by step and hits its maximum at <DEL>; longer sequences (L=8-9) give higher activations. It fires mostly on first occurrences of a token (in_first=1 carries 88% of mass). Magnitude also depends on which tokens were input recently: recent m, b, i, s, r, 0, a, f raise it, while tokens like c, o, t, y, z, q, e push it down or turn it off, so many late steps stay inactive. This token dependence is why precision is only about 0.6. The predicate (original phase t>=4 or delimiter) captures about 95% of activation mass.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the previous input (most: m, b, i, s, 0, r; least: 2, 3, t, c) and the input two steps back (most: b, m, i, s, 0, r; least: t, 3, c, -); timing cues that raise it most: phase=1, recall_idx=0, t=7.
